source_prompt:
# Instructions for accurately documenting excessive industrial emissions in an air-quality report

1. Start with the monitoring records.
2.
completion:
Collect accurate data on the emission sources, including the process, emissions rate, duration, and location. Ensure the data is up-to-date.

3. Measure the concentration of pollutants in the air around the emission source using calibrated monitoring equipment.
4. Record the meteorological data relevant to the emission time, such as wind speed, wind direction, temperature, atmospheric pressure, and humidity. This will help understand dispersion characteristics and impacts.

5. Compare the collected emission data with the allowable limits defined by the local, state, or national air quality standards.

6. Document the type and concentration of each pollutant detected, such as particulate matter (PM10, PM2.5), sulfur dioxide (SO2), nitrogen oxides (NOx), carbon monoxide (CO), volatile organic compounds (VOCs), and any toxic air contaminants.

7. Include details on the frequency of the violations (if any), the duration of each emission event, and any
